title: Risk Factors for End-Stage Glenohumeral Osteoarthritis
text:
Glenohumeral osteoarthritis is a leading cause of shoulder pain and disability, but a lack of investigation of
glenohumeral osteoarthritis risk factors has resulted in insufficient insights to guide evidence-based prevention
and treatment strategies. Our proposal aims to leverage multiple existing data resources to determine
associations of occupational exposures with osteoarthritis-related shoulder arthroplasty risk, identify genetic
variants associated with risk of osteoarthritis-related shoulder arthroplasty, and develop prediction models for
osteoarthritis-related shoulder arthroplasty. An understanding of glenohumeral osteoarthritis risk factors is
critically needed to inform design of prevention approaches, provide new insights into osteoarthritis etiology,
and to improve patient counseling in the future.

title: SCA7 neurodegeneration: Molecular epigenetic basis and therapy
text:
We have sought the basis of spinocerebellar ataxia type 7 (SCA7) neurodegeneration by focusing on
polyglutamine-expanded ataxin-7 transcription and epigenetic dysregulation, and after implicating DNA
damage, metabolic dysregulation, mitochondrial abnormalities, and calcium dyshomeostasis in SCA7 disease
pathogenesis, we are now performing single-cell transcriptome and epigenome analysis to define the cellular
and molecular processes underlying both the cone-rod dystrophy retinal degeneration and cerebellar
degeneration. Employing a novel Purkinje cell-enriched single nucleus (sn)RNA-seq method, we discovered
altered synaptic organization and dramatic dysregulation of normal aldolase-C / zebrin-II expression patterning,
and based upon analysis of related SCA polyQ disease model mice, altered cerebellar neurodevelopment is
emerging as a shared disease feature across various polyQ cerebellar ataxias. We now wish to continue this
line of investigation, and propose a series of experiments intended to identify DEGs and DARs from different
cell types to reveal genes and regulatory elements that underlie the molecular pathology in SCA7 retinal
degeneration and cerebellar degeneration, and then to determine the biological and physiological relevance of
delineated transcription factor alterations and epigenetic dysregulation by modulating the expression and
function of implicated factors in SCA7 knock-in model mice and by pursuing in vivo epigenetic rescue strategy
involving use of Cre-inducible dCas9-p300 (or -KRAB) mice to determine if such interventions can ameliorate
SCA7 retinal and cerebellar pathology, including disrupted zebrin-II patterning.

title: Kappa Opioid Receptor modulation of BLA inputs to the BNST and stress-escalated drinking
text:
This project will investigate the molecular mechanisms by which repeated exposure to an ethologically relevant
and common form of stress, social defeat stress, leads to persistent increases in alcohol consumption in both
males and females. Identification of such mechanisms could lead to better treatments for comorbid stress and
alcohol use disorders.

title: Multi-Modal Biomedical Data Fusion via Artificial Intelligence (AI)
text:
Integrating diverse data sources such as clinical tests, neuroimaging, and genetic information, our AI tools
aim to enhance diagnostic accuracy and uncover nuanced patterns, and subtypes not discernible by
traditional methods. The aims of the proposed projects are to develop AI tools that analyze multimodal
data (MRI, EEG, clinical tests) to improve diagnosis, predict disease progression, and discover subtypes
of psychosis. The approach involves machine learning for cross-sectional analysis, longitudinal analysis,
and population-level data analysis.

title: A Mobile Mindfulness-Based Intervention for Unhealthy Alcohol Use in People with Anxiety
text:
Unhealthy alcohol use is highly prevalent amongst individuals with chronic anxiety disorders, who are at
greater risk for alcohol-related harms and faster transition to alcohol use disorder. People with anxiety often
exhibit a relief-based drinking phenotype (i.e., drinking to alleviate negative affect); yet, current treatments fail
to target mechanisms that drive escalating alcohol use in this population. Enhanced understanding of
underlying mechanisms and optimal treatment strategies for relief-motivated drinking in people with anxiety will
help to reduce the burden of this significant public health problem on individuals, families, and communities.

title: Center for Collaboration on Climate and Community for Health (C4Health)
text: The public health relevance of our center, C4Health, lies in its unique ability to address the health effects of extreme weather on regional populations and local settings in the Midwest and Appalachia, and to identify and test promising interventions that could reduce morbidity and mortality due to extreme weather events. The rigorous research of this center will provide generalizable evidence that will also be applicable to other regions.

title: A noncanonical STING-dependent IFN-I independent pathway against KSHV reactivation
text:
Kaposi’s sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV) causes deadly cancers and establishes lifelong latent
infections, with reactivation producing infectious virions that pose a persistent oncogenic threat. Our preliminary
data reveal a previously unrecognized STING-dependent, IFN-I-independent host defense pathway that restricts
KSHV reactivation, mediated by IRF transcription factors and a subset of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs).
This R21 aims to define the molecular components and functional relevance of this pathway, providing
mechanistic insight, identifying novel antiviral targets, and laying the groundwork for future studies on innate
immunity and therapeutic strategies against KSHV.

title: Cellular and developmental genetic regulation of 3' isoform diversity in the human brain and its contribution to neuropsychiatric disorders
text:
Thousands of common genetic variants have now been robustly associated with neurodevelopmental and
psychiatric disorders, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and schizophrenia, yet translating these genetic
findings into a concrete understanding of the biological mechanisms underlying these disorders remains a major
obstacle hindering clinical translation. To interpret these findings, substantial efforts have been undertaken to
generate tissue- and cell-type-specific population-level functional genomic atlases linking genetic variants with
nearby alterations in gene expression, splicing, and isoform changes. Here, we seek to develop new methods
and resources to systematically characterize the regulation of alternative polyadenylation (APA) -- an
understudied yet critical cellular mechanism for gene regulation and trafficking -- during human brain
development and its contribution to neurodevelopmental and psychiatric disorders.

title: Regulation of T cell exhaustion via 3D chromatin architecture
text:
CD8+ T lymphocytes are essential players in mounting protective cellular immune responses against
pathogens and malignantly transformed cells. This proposal will mechanistically elucidate the regulatory
functions of three-dimensional genome topology and genome organizer protein CTCF in programming CD8+
T cell fate, differentiation, and lineage stability in response to chronic viral infection and tumor
microenvironment. Our proposed studies may lead to paradigm-shifting advances in scientific knowledge, and
provide novel insights into devising more effective vaccines and therapeutics for infectious diseases and
cancers.

title: Therapeutic Potential of Nucleotide Supplementation in Cardiac Repair
text:
Ischemic heart disease is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Cardiomyocyte proliferation
and cardiac repair hold great potential to treat ischemic heart disease. The primary objective and clinical
significance of this proposal are to investigate the mechanisms and therapeutic potential of nucleotide
balancing—a novel pathway implicated in cardiomyocyte proliferation—in promoting cardiac repair and thereby
conferring cardioprotection against ischemic injury.

title: An integrative genomics toolkit for rewriting regulatory DNA to reprogram gene expression
text:
This proposal aims to develop new methods to understand how regulatory DNA sequences quantitatively tune
gene expression in specific cell types, and how we can engineer these sequences to reprogram gene
expression. Our approach combines CRISPR technologies to rewrite genomic sequences with computational
models to predict which edits will have what effects. Our study will reveal new insights into gene regulation and
lay the foundations for future studies to develop CRISPR therapeutics for many diseases.

title: Exploiting a novel regulator of immunometabolism to enhance immunotherapy
text:
Harnessing the power of the T cell response to kill tumor cells is proving to be a highly effective anti-cancer
strategy. Most approaches focus on re-targeting T cells to better recognize tumor cells. In contrast our approach
focuses on improving the quality of the T cell response, to enable T cells to better persist and function in the
metabolically challenging environment of the tumor, and this can be layered upon potentially any T cell tumor-
targeting strategy.

title: Cancer Prevention and Control Research Training and Career Development Program
text: The sixth renewal of the University of Texas Health Science Center at Houston (UTHealth) School of Public Health training program builds on a 29-year track-record preparing fellows to become independent, skilled, and principled cancer control scientists. The training program is designed to prepare cancer prevention and control researchers to fill evidence gaps about multilevel causes of cancer outcomes; to develop and evaluate cancer control multilevel interventions (MLIs); and develop and test strategies to increase the adoption, implementation, sustainment, and scale up of effective interventions in community and health care settings. Ultimately, the long-term goal of the proposed training program is to reduce cancer morbidity and mortality and improve cancer outcomes.

title: HER3-PHF8 signaling axis in triple-negative breast cancer progression
text:
We aim to define the molecular basis of HER3 signaling promotion of triple negative breast cancer
(TNBC) progression and metastasis via upregulation of PHF8, a key histone lysine demethylase. The
proposed studies will shed a new light on our understanding of epigenetic promotion of HER3-driven TNBC.
Data generated will provide compelling evidence to develop novel therapeutic agents/strategies inhibiting
HER3 or PHF8 either alone or in combination with chemotherapy for the patients with TNBC, especially
those with the subtypes of Basal-like 1 (BL1), Luminal-Androgen receptor (LAR), or Basal-like 2 (BL2).

title: Identifying Undiagnosed Alzheimer’s Disease in Understudied Populations
text:
Despite the importance of a timely Alzheimer’s disease (AD) diagnosis, AD is underdiagnosed in real-world
community settings, particularly in understudied populations. Our objectives are to identify undiagnosed AD in
non-Hispanic white, Hispanic/Latino, and non-Hispanic African American groups utilizing disease trajectories
and genetics followed by validation and replication. Our contributions will enable the application of disease
trajectories in precision medicine and future work to reduce the bias of underdiagnosis in understudied
populations.

title: Cytomegalovirus-specific Immune Reconstitution after Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation in the Era of Modern Antiviral Prophylaxis
text:
Cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection causes an increased risk of complications and death after hematopoietic cell
transplantation. Recent studies suggest that new medications for the prevention of graft-versus-host disease
(GVHD) after transplant may promote the development of immunity against CMV; however, it is unclear whether
these new GVHD preventative drugs can promote CMV immunity in the era of modern CMV prevention. This
proposal will seek to answer this question, using cutting edge technology and analytical methods, in order to
inform management of CMV in the context of new and future cancer treatments.

title: Cardiomyocyte Non-autonomous Factors and Cardiac Regeneration in Large Mammals
text:
Myocardial infarction occurs in many types of congenital heart diseases and surgical treatments. Recent case
reports indicate that newborn patients may be able to regenerate myocardium and recover from severe
myocardial infarction that occurred shortly after birth. In this project, we will exploit the high regenerative
capacity of neonatal pig heart model to decipher the mechanisms of heart regeneration in large mammals.

title: Developing small molecule inhibitors of Pleckstrin-2 to treat thrombosis
text:
Thrombosis is a common complication and one of the leading causes of mortality and morbidity in patients with
myeloproliferative disorders. Our proposed study focuses on the development of small molecule inhibitors of a
novel drug target named Plek2 to treat thrombosis in these disorders, which will lay the foundation for future
clinical trials of new therapeutic strategies.

title: Organoid-immune cell culture modeling of therapeutic responses in cholangiocarcinoma
text:
Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) is a poorly understood liver malignancy that over the years has proven
highly refractory to both targeted therapies and immunotherapies. The lack of experimental models able to
faithfully recapitulate the genetic complexity of these tumors as well as accurately mimic patient-specific tumor-
cell interactions within the tumor microenvironment (TME) represent the major obstacle to the design of
combination strategies able to improves response to the current standard-of-care. In this proposal, we will
combine the use of multidimensional single cell analyses of human primary iCCAs with our newly developed
TME-reconstituted iCCA patient-derived organoid co-culture system to: 1) rigorously authenticate the functional
utility of our platform; 2) identify and validate underlying mechanisms of resistance to the current standard-of-
care chemoimmunotherapy; and 3) design novel combination strategies able to improve patient responses.

title: Diabetes-enhanced Experimental Periodontitis
text:
There is a close relationship between diabetes and periodontitis. Although this relationship is very
well documented we do not have a clear understanding of the mechanisms by which diabetes enhances the
severity and risk of periodontitis. We will investigate a novel mechanism that examines diabetes-altered
dendritic cell activity in contributing to periodontitis using state-of-the-art techniques.
